reproduction_target: Paired short-read (Illumina NovaSeq) and long-read (ONT PromethION R10.4.1) whole-genome analysis of one locally advanced rectal cancer patient (pre-treatment tumour, post-nCRT tumour, adjacent normals, matched blood): basecalling and alignment (Dorado/MinKNOW, minimap2, Trimmomatic, BWA-mem, samtools, GATK BQSR), QC (mosdepth, somalier), somatic SNV/indel calling (GATK Mutect2 with 1000G PoN + gnomAD; ClairS for ONT), variant normalization and annotation (bcftools, VEP v107 + COSMIC v95 filtering), cross-technology SNV/indel concordance (variant-ID matching, bedtools, GIAB homopolymer stratifications), force-calling of technology-private variants, genomic-context annotation (annotatr, AnnotationHub RepeatMasker), a multinomial logistic regression of discordance factors, structural-variant calling and comparison (Manta + convertInversion.py, Severus + WhatsHap, Minda, circlize, SpliceAI web lookup, ShatterSeek), somatic copy-number alteration calling (snp-pileup + facetsSuite/FACETS for Illumina; Wakhan for ONT), mutational-signature assignment (SigProfilerAssignment + COSMIC v3.4, including custom reformatting of Wakhan output into FACETS segmentation format and VCF-to-BEDPE conversion), and 5mC/5hmC methylation analysis (minimap2 realignment, Longphase + Sniffles phasing, modkit pileup, DSS differential methylation, bedtools feature intersection with UCSC/GeneHancer annotations, rGREAT enrichment). Clinical sample collection, HMW DNA extraction, DNA QC, ONT library preparation/sequencing and Illumina library preparation/sequencing at Novogene are wet-lab and out of computational-reproduction scope (counted in W).
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool/analysis-invocation derived from the METHODS subsections 'Oxford Nanopore whole genome sequencing', 'Illumina whole genome sequencing', 'Small somatic variant calling', 'Small variant concordance', 'Structural Variant calling', 'Somatic Copy Number Alterations', 'Mutational Signature Analysis' and 'Methylation analysis'. Coverage (mosdepth) and BAM post-processing (samtools) are kept as separate steps per technology because they operate on different inputs with different stated tool versions (samtools v1.9 for ONT vs v1.12 for Illumina). Unnamed custom analyses that the Methods describe but attribute to no tool (SNV-ID concordance matching, the multinomial logistic regression, the awk reformat of Wakhan output, VCF-to-BEDPE conversion, R visualisation) are scored as separate steps because they are load-bearing for reported results. NO code repository exists for this study's own analysis code, so no workflow file could be used as the objective granularity anchor. Wet-lab steps counted in W, not verdicted. Stage-1 prose-only: no code was read (there is none to read), and no A/B/C env_capture_class was assigned.

steps.label: ONT live basecalling with MinKNOW (v23.11.4) running Dorado (v7.2.13) in high-accuracy mode with 5mC and 5hmC modified-base calling enabled; reads with quality score < 7 discarded
Alignment of ONT FASTQ to GRCh38 with minimap2 (v2.26), settings '-ax map-ont'
Sorting and indexing of ONT BAM files with samtools (v1.9)
ONT genome coverage estimation with mosdepth (v0.3.3)
Sample-relatedness confirmation with somalier (v0.2.19) on both ONT and Illumina BAMs; sites VCF not stated

Illumina adapter trimming with Trimmomatic (v0.39) using a modified TruSeq2-PE.fa adapter file (Supplementary Materials File 1); parameters 'ILLUMINACLIP:<adapters.fa>:4:4:5:2:True LEADING:3 TRAILING:3 MINLEN:36'
Alignment of trimmed Illumina FASTQ to GRCh38 with BWA-mem (v0.7.17); no command-line parameters or read-group specification stated, GRCh38 build/patch/analysis-set not identified
Illumina BAM sorting, per-lane merging and indexing with samtools (v1.12)
Duplicate marking (MarkDuplicates) and base quality score recalibration (BaseRecalibrator, ApplyBQSR) with GATK (v4.5.0.0); known-sites resources for BQSR not stated
Illumina genome coverage assessment with mosdepth (v0.3.3)

Somatic small-variant calling in Illumina WGS with Mutect2 (GATK v4.3.0.0), tumour/adjacent-normal vs matched blood, supplying the 1000 Genomes panel of normals (1000g_pon.hg38.vcf.gz) and the gnomAD germline resource (af-only-gnomad.hg38.vcf.gz); resource file names given but no release/version or download source

Contamination estimation and Mutect2 filtering: GATK (v4.3.0.0) GetPileupSummaries and CalculateContamination using ExAC common germline variants (small_exac_common_3.hg38.vcf.gz), then FilterMutectCalls; no thresholds or non-default options stated
Splitting the filtered Mutect2 VCF into SNVs and indels using 'bcftools view'; bcftools version stated nowhere in the paper and no expression/flags given

Somatic SNV/indel calling in ONT WGS with ClairS (v0.4.0), tumour/adjacent-normal vs matched blood; parameters '--platform ont_r10_dorado_hac_5khz --enable-indel-calling --enable_clair3_germline_output --q8 --longphase_for_phasing'; post-filters = chr1-22,X,Y, PASS, depth >= 4 in both tissue and germline, indels > 50bp removed

Variant normalization and ID assignment: multiallelic splitting with 'bcftools norm', indel left-alignment with GATK (v4.3.0.0) LeftAlignAndTrimVariants, unique IDs '<chrom>:<pos>:<ref>:<alt>' via 'bcftools annotate'; bcftools version never stated, annotate expression not given

Annotation of small somatic variants with Variant Effect Predictor (VEP v107), then filter_vep against COSMIC (v95) with filter expression '(Existing_variation match COS or not Existing_variant)'; VEP cache/assembly version and COSMIC download not further specified

Cross-technology SNV concordance determination by exact variant-ID matching (chromosome, position, reference and alternate allele must agree) and VAF computation as alt depth / total depth; performed by unnamed custom code with no script, language or version stated

Indel concordance and homopolymer overlap assessment with bedtools (v2.30.0) under three schemes: reciprocal complete overlap ('-f 1 -r'), default 1bp minimum overlap, and 1bp overlap within a 5bp window ('slop -b 5'); GIAB simple-repeat homopolymer stratifications (GRCh38_SimpleRepeat_homopolymer_*_slop5.bed.gz) from https://github.com/usnistgov/giab-stratifications, no release version or commit given
Re-evaluation of Mutect2-private SNVs in ONT data via a second ClairS (v0.4.0) run with '--genotyping_mode_vcf_fn' supplying the private-SNV VCF and '--phase_tumor' re-enabled
Force-calling of ClairS-private SNVs in Illumina data with Mutect2 via the '--alleles' option

Genomic-region annotation of SNVs with the annotatr R package (v1.24.0) using annotations 'hg38_genes_1to5kb', 'hg38_genes_exons', 'hg38_genes_promoters', 'hg38_genes_introns', 'hg38_genes_intergenic'
Annotation of SNVs with repetitive regions using RepeatMasker hg38 tracks retrieved through the AnnotationHub R package (v3.6.0); AnnotationHub snapshot date and record ID not stated

Multinomial logistic regression of factors contributing to SNV discordance (tumour purity, repetitive region, strand bias, germline VAF), reported in the Abstract and Results; no software, package, version, model formula, covariate coding or fitting procedure is given anywhere in Methods

Structural-variant calling in Illumina WGS with Manta (v1.6.0) using default parameters, followed by the supplementary convertInversion.py script to reformat inversion entries; PASS + chr1-22,X,Y filtering
Phasing of ONT BAMs with WhatsHap (v1.7) haplotag, supplying phased germline SNVs output by ClairS to keep phasing consistent across samples

Structural-variant calling in ONT WGS with Severus (v1.3) using phased tumour and germline BAMs plus the phased germline VCF, and tandem-repeat regions (human_GRCh38_no_alt_analysis_set.trf.bed.gz) via '--vntr-bed'; PASS + chr1-22,X,Y filtering. Source/version of the TRF bed not stated
Cross-technology structural-variant comparison with Minda (https://github.com/KolmogorovLab/minda, commit 2066ef5) using default parameters - the only commit-level pin in the paper
Circos plot generation with the circlize R package (v0.4.15); plotting script and R version not stated

Splicing-effect prediction for structural variants using the online SpliceAI lookup (https://spliceailookup.broadinstitute.org/, accessed 31/07/2025); no tool/model version, no transcript set, no score threshold, no batch interface - a manual web-service step
Chromothripsis detection with ShatterSeek (v1.1); input SV/CN preparation, chromosome set and calling criteria not stated
Base-level coverage pileup generation for FACETS with snp-pileup (v0.6.2), parameters '-q15 -Q20 -P100 -r25,0', using a common-SNP file obtained from dbSNP build 151

Somatic copy-number alteration calling on Illumina WGS with FACETS (v0.6.2) driven by facetsSuite (https://github.com/mskcc/facets-suite, v2.0.9) script run_facets_wrapper.R; wrapper arguments (cval, purity/ploidy settings, seed) not stated

Somatic copy-number alteration calling on ONT WGS with Wakhan (https://github.com/KolmogorovLab/Wakhan, v0.1.0) from haplotagged BAMs, options '--normal-phased-vcf', '--breakpoints' (Severus SVs), '--copy-numbers-subclonal-enable', '--loh-enable', purity range 0-0.60, and a FACETS gene list via 'user-input-genes'
Mutational-signature assignment for SBS, indel, copy-number and SV signatures with SigProfilerAssignment (v0.1.8) against COSMIC v3.4

Custom reformatting of ONT copy-number output for signature analysis: haplotype-specific bed files from Wakhan combined 'using awk' and modified to replicate the FACETS segmentation format, with segments flanking centromeres extended to fill centromeric gaps (Wakhan v0.1.0 does not call CN in centromeres); no script, no awk expression, no centromere coordinate source
Preparation of SV signature input: Manta and Severus output VCFs filtered for PASS and converted to BEDPE format by unnamed means (no tool, script or version stated)

Methylation read preparation: unmapped modified-base BAMs from MinKNOW sorted by read name and merged, converted to FASTQ with '-T *' to carry all tags, realigned to GRCh38 with minimap2 (v2.26) '-ax map-ont -y', coordinate-sorted, reads with MAPQ < 20 removed; samtools version for this branch not stated
Haplotagging of methyl-BAMs with Longphase (v1.7.3) haplotag using germline SNVs from ClairS and structural variants from Sniffles (v2.6.0); Sniffles invocation parameters not stated
Generation of bedmethyl files with modkit (https://github.com/nanoporetech/modkit, v0.5.0) pileup, filtered to autosomes and sex chromosomes; pileup options (mod thresholds, --cpg, --ref) not stated

Differential methylation/hydroxymethylation detection with the DSS R package (v2.54.0): DMLtest() with smoothing enabled (single-replicate analysis), callDMR() with minlen=100, minCG=15, dis.merge=100, delta 15% for DMRs and 5% for DhMRs

Linking differentially modified regions to genomic features with 'bedtools intersect' (bedtools v2.30.0 stated earlier in Methods) using canonical-transcript coordinates (knownGene, exons, introns), RepeatMasker and CpG-island tracks for GRCh38 obtained from the UCSC table browser; promoters defined as -2kb/+200bp around the TSS. UCSC track download date/version and intersect flags not stated

Enhancer annotation from GeneHancer (v5.24), restricted to elite-status elements classed as enhancers or enhancer/promoters; the GeneHancer distribution is licence-restricted and the selection/intersection was done with unnamed code

Functional enrichment of differentially modified genomic regions with rGREAT (v2.9.2) using gene-extended windows and UCSC knownGene transcription start sites, against Hallmark MSigDB gene sets; MSigDB release version, background/universe and significance thresholds not stated

Visualisation in R of copy-number profiles, mutational-signature contributions and mutational matrices ('visualised using R', 'Copy number profiles were visualised using R'); no R version, no packages, no scripts

Clinical sample collection: pre-treatment primary tumour biopsy, adjacent normal tissue and matched blood at baseline; post-treatment primary tumour and adjacent normal at surgical resection (5 samples, ethics 13/82 and 15/09)
High molecular weight DNA extraction following the ONT Rabbit Liver DNA extraction protocol, substituting the QIAGEN Blood and Cell Culture DNA Mini Kit for the Midi Kit
DNA quantification (Qubit dsDNA Broad Range Assay Kit, Invitrogen) and quality assessment (Bioanalyser DNA 1000 kit, Agilent)
ONT library preparation with the Ligation Sequencing Kit SQK-LSK114 per manufacturer protocol
ONT sequencing on R10.4.1 PromethION flow cells (FLO-PRO144M) on a PromethION 2 Solo, 72h runtime per flow cell, with washes and reloads as needed
Illumina library preparation and paired-end sequencing on a NovaSeq 6000 at Novogene

headline.static_readiness: 0/44 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: 35/44 (80%) readiness upper bound (n(R-star)+n(RI))/|S| - 'ready for a reproduction attempt', never 'reproducible'. This paper is an unusually well-pinned prose description with NO code artifact at all: 30+ tools are named with exact versions (minimap2 v2.26, ClairS v0.4.0, GATK v4.5.0.0/v4.3.0.0, Manta v1.6.0, Severus v1.3, FACETS v0.6.2 via facetsSuite v2.0.9, Wakhan v0.1.0, SigProfilerAssignment v0.1.8, DSS v2.54.0, modkit v0.5.0, rGREAT v2.9.2, and one true commit pin - Minda commit 2066ef5), and many steps quote full command-line flags. But there is no GitHub/GitLab/Zenodo repository, no workflow file, no conda environment, no container, and no R/Python runtime version anywhere. Under the Delta-2 symmetric env-closure gate, scattered exact pins in prose without interpreter/channel/platform closure cap Version at 1, so 0 steps can reach R-star even in principle at stage 1, and a stage-2 code check would find nothing to check. The 9 non-RI steps are the ones where prose stops naming tools: bcftools invocations with no version (C13, C15), the SNV-ID concordance matching (C17), the multinomial logistic regression that is a headline Abstract result but has zero methodological description (C23), the manual SpliceAI web lookup (C29), the awk reformat of Wakhan output into FACETS segmentation format including the centromere gap-filling heuristic (C35), the VCF-to-BEDPE conversion (C36), the GeneHancer elite-element selection (C42), and R visualisation (C44). Data is the second binding constraint: the genomic data are patient WGS under EGA controlled access, but the statement is prospective ('will be available') and cites only a Data Access Committee id (EGAC00001001585), not a dataset or study accession, so Data scores 1 (missing id) rather than 2 (controlled-access legitimate with resolving accession) on every step.
headline.coverage: 44 computational steps assessed from Methods prose (computational coverage 44/50 = 88%); 6 wet-lab steps counted in W and not verdicted (sample collection, HMW DNA extraction, DNA QC, ONT library prep, ONT PromethION sequencing, Illumina library prep + NovaSeq sequencing at Novogene). The paper has a 'DATA ACCESS' section; it has NO code-availability statement of any kind. All step evidence comes from the METHODS section of the JATS full text.

gaps.missing: There is NO code availability statement and NO repository. The paper's only availability statement is 'DATA ACCESS'. No GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket/Zenodo/Software Heritage URL for this study's own analysis code appears anywhere in the article; the only repository URLs cited are third-party tool homepages (giab-stratifications, KolmogorovLab/minda, KolmogorovLab/Wakhan, mskcc/facets-suite, nanoporetech/modkit). No workflow file (Snakemake/Nextflow/WDL/CWL/Makefile), no driver scripts, no parameter configs are deposited. Every step is reconstructable at best (Code axis capped at 1 for all 44 steps).
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the analysis code - even a flat directory of the shell/R/Python scripts actually run - in a public repository, archive a tagged release to Zenodo for a DOI, and add a Code Availability statement citing it.

gaps.where: All sequencing data underlying every computational step (5 samples x 2 technologies: ONT PromethION and Illumina NovaSeq WGS)
gaps.missing: The DATA ACCESS statement reads verbatim: 'The genomic datasets generated in this study will be available from European Genome-Phenome Archive for academic use through the Genomic Oncology Research Group Data Access Committee (EGAC00001001585).' This is future tense ('will be available') and cites only a DAC identifier - there is no EGAS study accession, no EGAD dataset accession, no submission date, and no statement that the data are currently deposited. Controlled access for patient WGS is legitimate and not penalized in itself, but the absence of a resolving dataset accession means the DAC route cannot be exercised today. No intermediate artifacts (BAMs, VCFs, bedmethyl files, per-variant concordance tables, copy-number segmentation files) are deposited either.
gaps.how_to_close: Complete the EGA submission and publish the EGAS/EGAD accessions plus the DAC application procedure and expected turnaround. Additionally deposit derived, non-identifying intermediates (filtered somatic VCFs, CN segment tables, DMR tables) so downstream steps can be re-run without a DAC application.

gaps.where: Software environment for all 44 computational steps
gaps.missing: No conda environment file, lockfile, container image, requirements.txt or renv.lock exists (there is no repository to hold one). No interpreter/runtime version is stated anywhere: R version is never given despite eight R packages being used (annotatr v1.24.0, AnnotationHub v3.6.0, circlize v0.4.15, ShatterSeek v1.1, facetsSuite v2.0.9, FACETS v0.6.2, DSS v2.54.0, rGREAT v2.9.2), and Python version is never given despite SigProfilerAssignment v0.1.8, ClairS v0.4.0 and Wakhan v0.1.0. Bioconductor release is not stated. This is the classic exact_pins_partial pattern: excellent per-tool pinning, zero environment closure, so Version caps at 1 on every step.
gaps.how_to_close: Ship a conda-lock/pixi.lock or a container with a recorded digest covering the interpreter, channels and platform, and state the resolved R/Bioconductor and Python versions.

gaps.where: C13, C15 (bcftools view / norm / annotate), C37 (samtools in the methylation branch), C35 (awk), C44 (R)
gaps.missing: bcftools is used for three load-bearing operations (SNV/indel splitting, multiallelic normalization, variant-ID assignment) but its version is never stated anywhere in the paper - unlike samtools, which is pinned twice (v1.9 ONT, v1.12 Illumina) but is left unversioned in the methylation branch. awk implementation (GNU awk vs BSD awk, which differ) and R version are also unstated.
gaps.how_to_close: State bcftools, samtools (methylation branch), awk and R versions alongside the others.

gaps.where: C17 (SNV-ID concordance matching), C23 (multinomial logistic regression), C35 (Wakhan-to-FACETS reformat + centromere gap filling), C36 (VCF to BEDPE conversion), C44 (R visualisation)
gaps.missing: Five analyses that produce reported results are attributed to no tool and no deposited script. Most consequential is C23: the multinomial logistic regression is quoted in the Abstract as identifying tumour purity, repetitive-region membership, strand bias and germline VAF as discordance factors, yet Methods contains no model specification, no software, no covariate coding, no reference category and no fit diagnostics - the Methods section does not mention the regression at all. C35 additionally encodes a substantive analytical decision (extending segments flanking centromeres to avoid false homozygous deletions) with no stated centromere coordinate source or extension rule.
gaps.how_to_close: Describe the regression fully (package, formula, encoding, reference level, sample size, outputs) and deposit the custom concordance / reformatting / plotting scripts.

gaps.where: C1/C2/C7/C37 (GRCh38 reference), C11/C12 (1000G PoN, gnomAD af-only, ExAC common), C16 (VEP cache, COSMIC v95), C18 (GIAB stratifications), C22 (AnnotationHub RepeatMasker), C26 (TRF bed), C31 (dbSNP build 151), C34 (COSMIC v3.4 signatures), C41 (UCSC knownGene/RepeatMasker/CpG tracks), C42 (GeneHancer v5.24), C43 (Hallmark MSigDB)
gaps.missing: External reference resources are consumed throughout, and the pinning quality is inconsistent. Some are versioned in prose (COSMIC v95 and v3.4, dbSNP build 151, GeneHancer v5.24, VEP v107). Others are named only by filename or track name with no release, download date or checksum: the GRCh38 build/patch/analysis-set is never identified even though it determines alignment coordinates; the GATK resource bundle files (1000g_pon.hg38.vcf.gz, af-only-gnomad.hg38.vcf.gz, small_exac_common_3.hg38.vcf.gz) have no bundle version; the GIAB stratification release is not given (only the repo URL); human_GRCh38_no_alt_analysis_set.trf.bed.gz has no source; AnnotationHub has no snapshot date; UCSC table-browser downloads have no date; MSigDB Hallmark has no release. Because there is no workflow to inspect, no env_capture_class (A/B/C) can be assigned - all remain 'n/a' at stage 1, and every one of these would at best be class B (pin-in-prose-only) even if code existed.
gaps.how_to_close: Record the exact reference-genome analysis set, GATK bundle version, GIAB stratification release, AnnotationHub snapshot, UCSC download dates and MSigDB release, ideally as versioned download rules inside a workflow rather than prose.

gaps.where: C1 (MinKNOW v23.11.4 / Dorado v7.2.13 basecalling), C16 (COSMIC v95 via filter_vep), C34 (COSMIC v3.4 signatures), C42 (GeneHancer v5.24)
gaps.missing: Several dependencies are vendor-controlled or licence-gated: MinKNOW/Dorado are ONT-distributed and the specific basecalling model file behind 'high accuracy mode' with 5mC/5hmC at the stated version is not named; COSMIC requires a licensed account for academic download; GeneHancer full data are distributed under restricted licence via GeneCards. These are pinned by version (so Version=1 rather than 0) but re-acquisition is not unconditional.
gaps.how_to_close: Name the exact Dorado basecalling model identifier (e.g. dna_r10.4.1_e8.2_400bps_hac@vX.Y.Z_5mCG_5hmCG) and state the licence/access route used for COSMIC and GeneHancer.

gaps.missing: Several steps are stochastic or optimization-based (FACETS segmentation depends on a random SNP-thinning seed and on cval; SigProfilerAssignment uses NNLS with bootstrap resampling; Wakhan subclonal CN inference searches purity/ploidy space over a stated 0-0.60 purity range). No random seed is reported for any of them, so exact re-derivation of the published segment boundaries and signature contributions cannot be guaranteed - only distributional agreement.
gaps.how_to_close: Report and fix random seeds, and state the FACETS cval and SigProfilerAssignment bootstrap settings.

gaps.missing: The splicing-effect analysis was performed through the interactive Broad SpliceAI lookup web page, accessed 31/07/2025. There is no scriptable interface record, no model or annotation version, no transcript set, no delta-score threshold, and no list of the variants submitted. This sub-analysis is externalized to a service whose state at the access date cannot be recovered.
gaps.how_to_close: Re-run with the installable SpliceAI release (stating model and annotation version, transcript set and delta-score cutoff) and deposit the input variant list and output table.
